review_evidence: Each reviewed candidate gives the same critical-line assertion for nontrivial zeta zeros; the three records are duplicate formulations, not separate targets.
All reviewed records ask whether rational Hodge classes on complex projective varieties arise from algebraic cycles, matching the Top 500 target.
The reviewed records identify Mordell-Weil rank with L-function vanishing order at one; the number-field formulation includes the rational-field target.
The candidate formulations use the same smooth-projective coniveau and support description as the generalized Hodge target.
The candidates concern maximal values or zeros of derivatives of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions, not the uniform real zero-free interval in the Top 500 target.
Reviewed motivic formulations equate period transcendence degree and motivic Galois dimension, including the motive-over-Q formulation used by the target.
Two candidates explicitly assert non-density of number-field rational points on varieties of general type, which is the stated Bombieri-Lang endpoint.
Reviewed candidates restrict to algebraic K-theory and in places to torsion-free or hyperbolic groups, while the Top 500 target jointly requires K- and L-theory assembly for every group.
Candidates state continuum or usual-limit condensation questions but do not fix the Top 500 three-dimensional interacting low-temperature off-diagonal-long-range-order scope.
The reviewed candidates give the two standard effective-Mordell endpoints: explicit height control and a terminating determination of rational points on genus-at-least-two curves.
Reviewed records state the same two-real-number liminf product condition, with one using an equivalent Diophantine-system formulation.
Both candidates impose the one-quarter lower spectral bound for congruence quotients, matching the Top 500 eigenvalue formulation.
The candidates directly ask for superpolynomial, in particular exponential, lower bounds for Frege proofs of explicit tautologies.
Each reviewed record states infinitely many consecutive-prime gaps of every positive even size, exactly the Polignac target.
The hyperbolic-knot candidate uses the colored Jones root-of-unity asymptotic and complement volume specified by the Top 500 target; broader knot/link versions are duplicates or extensions.
The general closed-aspherical positive-scalar-curvature candidate has the same assertion; the dimension-at-least-four versions are restricted duplicate formulations.
The closest candidate covers compact congruence surfaces, whereas the Top 500 target ranges over arithmetic locally symmetric spaces; billiard quantum ergodicity is a separate setting.
Arzhantseva's candidate asks whether every Gromov-hyperbolic group is residually finite, precisely the finite-quotient separation property in the target.
Reviewed candidates uniformly bound rational points of fixed-genus curves over a number field, matching the target and its equivalent degree-based presentation.
The candidates formulate Frobenius equidistribution in the Sato-Tate group for abelian varieties over number fields, including arbitrary dimension.
Both records ask for nonvanishing of the p-adic regulator, the standard zero-defect Leopoldt formulation.
The candidates propose structural hypotheses about extremal subtour-LP solutions, while the Top 500 target is the distinct numerical assertion that the full metric-TSP gap equals four-thirds.
Reviewed candidates concern an anharmonic-oscillator analogue and a negative-order mapping problem, not the all-dimension Euclidean nonnegative-order Lp characterization.
Candidates extend or specialize homological fixed-point questions to homeomorphisms or circle actions; the Top 500 target is the classical Crit(M) bound for all Hamiltonian diffeomorphisms.
Pair correlation and asymptotic simplicity assertions concern distributional zero behavior, whereas the target requires simplicity of every nontrivial zeta zero.
One candidate directly states pseudo-effective log-canonical divisor nonvanishing; the abundance candidates are nearby stronger or adjacent formulations.
The Falconer candidate has the same Hausdorff-dimension threshold and positive-measure distance-set conclusion; the critical-threshold wording is an equivalent boundary formulation.
The unit and analytic-injectivity conjectures are distinct torsion-free group-ring assertions; neither is the field-group-ring domain claim in the Top 500 target.
The leading candidate uses the same common-resolution canonical-divisor condition and derives derived-category equivalence; converse and L-equivalence entries are adjacent variants.
All reviewed candidates give the polylogarithmic Cayley-graph diameter bound for finite nonabelian simple groups and arbitrary generators.
The candidates ask for the minimum unit-distance coloring number of the Euclidean plane, exactly the Hadwiger-Nelson target.
The leading log-Calabi-Yau cone-conjecture formulation includes effective nef and movable cones with rational-polyhedral fundamental domains; weak and arithmetic versions are related restatements.
Michel's candidate identifies a simple compact metric from its boundary distance function up to boundary-fixing isometry, matching the target.
Both candidates extend the Euclidean isoperimetric inequality to complete simply connected nonpositively curved manifolds, the Cartan-Hadamard statement.
The candidate explicitly asks whether the Euler-Mascheroni constant is irrational; the transcendence candidate is a stronger adjacent conjecture.
Both candidates ask whether complements of finite first-order spectra are spectra, equivalently the stated finite-spectrum problem.
The candidates concern an ell-q matrix formulation and a broader Dirichlet-polynomial conjecture, while the target fixes the separated-large-values exponent bound and parameter regime.
The leading genericity candidate has the same generic closed-hypersurface setting and spherical or cylindrical singularity models; other entries are refinements.
Both candidates ask for an algorithm deciding whether a red-blue bipartite graph has a perfect matching with exactly k red edges; the Top 500 target makes polynomial time explicit.
The leading candidate asks precisely for an invariant finitely additive probability measure on Thompson group F; weak amenability is a distinct adjacent question.
The leading candidate requests a combinatorial interpretation of the same Kronecker multiplicities for all triples of partitions; the efficient-description entry is adjacent.
Reviewed candidates are polynomial-time recognition problems for graph width, clique graphs, or slack matrices, not recognition of the unknot from a knot encoding.
All reviewed records state that the real-topology closure of rational points has finitely many connected components, matching Mazur's target.
Each candidate has the two-by-two rational-linear-independence hypothesis and the conclusion that one exponential product is transcendental.
Both candidates seek minimum-energy configurations of finitely many mutually repelling charges on the unit sphere, the Thomson problem.
The leading records state the same Hanf-threshold categoricity transfer for L_omega1,omega; the lambda-plus generalization is adjacent.
The candidate's Turing-degree classification by iterates of jump is the standard Martin-conjecture core; the Top 500 entry makes its determinacy and cone scope explicit.
Candidates state that Kazhdan-Lusztig polynomials depend only on the Bruhat interval's combinatorial isomorphism type, matching the target.
The candidates concern particular K_s,t-free surplus and K_2,t degree regimes, while the target asks the full fixed-t extremal asymptotic for K_t,t-free bipartite graphs.
The cellular-automaton candidate gives the all-group injective-implies-surjective assertion; the countable formulation is a restricted duplicate.
The leading candidate asks exactly whether every connected vertex-transitive graph has a Hamiltonian path; cycle and strong forms are extra context.
Reviewed candidates impose per-boundary-component flux conditions or specialize to the planar case, whereas the target isolates the three-dimensional total-flux-only weak-existence question.
The leading candidate states exactly that ab=1 implies ba=1 in a group ring over any field and any group; countability is only a restricted duplicate.
All reviewed records use balanced trivial-group presentations and Nielsen/conjugation moves to reach the trivial presentation, matching the Andrews-Curtis target.
